_adapter_note: Adapted from Markdown to threatmodel/0.1. Fields present in source are mapped; fields not present in source are omitted or marked N/A. No ATT&CK IDs in original — left empty.

trust_boundaries: Caller to axios: fully trusted — malicious callers are a non-goal
Axios to network: everything past the socket is untrusted
Environment variables (proxy settings): trusted but pivot in CI/container scenarios
Caller-supplied hooks (interceptors, transforms, adapters): full privilege, not sandboxed
architecture_summary.operational_context: npm library — runtime (applications importing axios) + project/SDLC (package build and publish pipeline)

threat_actors.name: Malicious server / on-path attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Credential theft, data exfiltration, SSRF pivot to internal network
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Control of upstream server or network path
non_capabilities: Cannot modify axios source at runtime without supply chain compromise
No physical access to caller environment

threat_actors.name: Drive-by contributor
threat_actors.motivation: Inject malicious code into npm package via PR
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Fork and pull request to public GitHub repo
non_capabilities: No write access to main branch without review
No access to npm publish token or maintainer secrets
Cannot bypass OIDC publish flow without GitHub Actions compromise

threat_actors.name: Compromised maintainer account
threat_actors.motivation: Publish malicious package version, supply chain compromise
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Phishing, credential theft, or workstation compromise
non_capabilities: Cannot bypass npm provenance attestation without GitHub Actions control
Cannot retroactively alter published provenance attestations

attack_paths.impact: Pivot to internal network, access metadata services, scan internal hosts
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Caller fully controls URL; axios does not validate URL safety

attack_paths.impact: Authorization headers sent to attacker-controlled redirect target
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: follow-redirects strips headers; sensitiveHeaders config available but not default
Residual risk very low after GHSA-445q-vr5w-6q77 fix

attack_paths.impact: Property injection affecting downstream code behavior
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Key filtering in merge helpers; hasOwnProp guards on config reads

attack_paths.technique_name: Sensitive data in error objects and logs
attack_paths.entry_point: Uncaught axios error propagated to application logger
attack_paths.impact: Credentials, tokens, or request bodies exposed in error logs
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Documented known risk; config object included in errors by design

attack_paths.entry_point: Fork pull request to public repository
attack_paths.impact: Malicious code merged to main branch, eventually published in npm release
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Single maintainer — no two-person review; dist/ hard to review

attack_paths.technique_name: Dev dependency compromise of maintainer workstation
attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious update to Rollup, Babel, Vitest, or ESLint plugin
attack_paths.impact: Build process executes attacker code with full maintainer privileges; npm credentials exfiltrated
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Build-tool plugins execute during local builds; not isolated

attack_paths.impact: Full control of GitHub repo and npm publish capability
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Hardware key policy not verifiable from repo; backup keys needed

mitigations.control_name: sensitiveHeaders config to strip headers on redirect
Key filtering in merge helpers + hasOwnProp guards
npm ci --ignore-scripts in CI; project .npmrc ignore-scripts=true
OIDC publishing with no NPM_TOKEN; npm provenance attestations
SHA-pinned GitHub Actions; minimal workflow permissions; zizmor linting
Dependabot with 7-day cooldown; tag protection rules
Document sensitive data in errors as known risk; no automated redaction

findings.severity_rationale: SSRF is high likelihood (caller controls URL) and high impact (internal network pivot). Axios explicitly treats this as caller responsibility — residual risk is substantial.
Sensitive data in errors: high likelihood (errors are common), medium-high impact (credentials in logs). Documented but no automated fix.
Malicious contributor PR: high likelihood (public repo, single maintainer), critical impact (supply chain compromise affecting all axios consumers).
Dev dependency workstation compromise: medium likelihood, critical impact (full build-time code execution with npm publish access).
Credential leak on redirect: medium likelihood, high impact if auth headers reach attacker server.
